scenes.title: Stress: important content words
scenes.narration: Step three: stress. Emphasise key content words, not every word. The purple highlights show phenomenon, bioluminescence, organisms, produce light, chemical reactions and illumination. These carry the main meaning. Make them slightly stronger while keeping the smaller connecting words light and natural.

scenes.title: Chunk: meaningful phrases
scenes.narration: Step two: chunk. Divide the long scientific sentence into meaningful phrases, as the coloured highlights show. Pause briefly between chunks, for example after bioluminescence, marine organisms, produce light, and chemical reactions. Read each chunk smoothly instead of stopping after every word.

scenes.title: Five scientific sentences for practice
scenes.narration: Here are five difficult scientific sentences for practice. They introduce bioluminescence, nanotechnology, photosynthetic efficiency, neuroplasticity, and thermodynamic properties. Preview each sentence, identify unfamiliar words, then practise pronunciation, chunking and stress. Apply the same five-step method to all five examples.

scenes.title: Connect: natural flow
scenes.narration: Step four: connect. Link words naturally instead of sounding robotic. The blue highlights show phrases that should flow together. Use smooth transitions within each phrase, then pause naturally where the meaning changes. Keep your speech clear, controlled and conversational.

scenes.title: Finish: controlled ending
scenes.narration: Step five: finish. Maintain a steady pace all the way to the last word. Don't rush or trail off at the end. In this example, complete the final phrase, external source of illumination, clearly. Finish with control, not a sudden stop.

scenes.title: Preview: difficult words
scenes.narration: Step one: preview. Scan the sentence before speaking and identify difficult words. Here, they are bioluminescence, organisms and illumination. Prepare their pronunciation, then begin reading. This quick check helps prevent hesitation and makes your delivery more confident.

scenes.title: The five-step formula
scenes.narration: Here's the complete formula: stop reading word by word. Preview difficult words, chunk sentences into phrases, stress important content words, connect words naturally, and finish clearly at a steady pace. Practise these five steps together to improve your P T E Read Aloud fluency.
